items.t: Was against establishing a new National Bank of the United States, vetoing the bill to create one.
items.q: Tyler vetoes a second bill for the establishment of a National Bank of the United States

record.t: Signed the joint resolution to annex Texas.
record.q: President John Tyler signed a joint resolution to annex Texas.

record.t: Submitted the joint resolution to annex Texas, which Congress passed.
record.q: Congress passes the joint resolution (which only requires a simple majority by both houses) submitted by Tyler to annex Texas.

record.t: Chose Caleb Cushing as his representative in treaty negotiations with the Chinese, and Cushing and his counterparts reached the terms of the Treaty of Wangxia, signed in 1844.
record.q: U.S. President John Tyler chose Massachusetts Congressman Caleb Cushing as his representative in treaty negotiations with the Chinese. Cushing and his counterparts reached the terms of the treaty quickly and signed it at Wangxia, a suburb of the Portuguese port city of Macau, in 1844.

record.t: Appointed Henry Wise as Minister to Brazil (1844).
record.q: In 1844, President Tyler appointed him Minister to Brazil, where he served until 1847.

record.t: Appointed John C. Calhoun as Secretary of State (1844).
record.q: John Caldwell Calhoun was appointed Secretary of State by President John Tyler on March 6, 1844.

record.t: Vetoed a second bill to establish a National Bank; his whole cabinet except Secretary of State Daniel Webster resigned.
record.q: resigns after Tyler vetoes a second bill for the establishment of a National Bank

record.t: Became the first vice president to assume the presidency on a president's death, after William Henry Harrison died, setting the precedent for succession.
record.q: He is the first ever to do so, setting the precedent for presidential succession.

record.t: Took the presidential oath of office after President Harrison's death and claimed he had succeeded to the presidency for the remainder of Harrison's term (1841).
record.q: Vice President John Tyler took the presidential oath of office and claimed that he had succeeded to the presidency automatically for the remainder of Harrison's term by operation of Article II, Section 1, Clause 6.

record.t: Vetoed Clay's bill to establish a National Bank, and vetoed a similar bank bill passed by Congress.
record.q: Tyler vetoed Clay's bill to establish a National Bank with branches in several states. A similar bank bill was passed by Congress. But again, on states' rights grounds, Tyler vetoed it.
